text:
alex: infra-bot alert: p99 gen latency spiked to ~1.8s on pool us-west-2-gpu-a, throughput down ~30% — graph: https://grafana.redwood/board/latency?panel=gen

infra-bot: ALERT: inference.p99 > 1.5s for 5m on cluster us-west-2-gpu-a. sample traces attached.

priya: seeing this too. did we flip any kernel selector flags in that pool last night?

maria: quick profile attached (short):
```
flamegraph summary: hot path -> attention_kernel_v1 -> matmul -> cuda_sync
hot function: kernel_selector.py:410 select_kernel_for(seq_len=avg~1200, tokens=14000)
observation: selector picks 'attn_v1' when seq_len > 1024, but our sampling misclassified many streaming sessions as "long" due to toolcall prefixes
```

sam: kv cache eviction spikes correlate: evict_count +420% in the same window, cache hitrate dropped from 0.74 -> 0.31

jun: one tenant (acme-inc) shows tool-calling loop generating long expanded prompts repeatedly, many streaming sessions blocked in the queue. sample log:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:31Z] tenant=acme-inc req_id=abc123 prompt_tokens=13892 tool_calls=67 streaming=true
```
looks like streaming backpressure + long prompt = batch imbalance -> selector picks big-kernel -> high allocation overhead

alex: proposed immediate mitigations:
- pin kernel selection to safe_kernel=v2 for us-west-2-gpu-a (lower startup overhead)
- increase batching timeout from 6ms -> 12ms (reduce tiny-batch pressure)
- throttle tenant acme-inc to 30rps until we verify
commands:
```
rzctl pool update --pool us-west-2-gpu-a --kernel-policy=pinned:v2
rzctl config set batching.timeout_ms 12 --pool us-west-2-gpu-a
rzctl tenant throttle --tenant acme-inc --rps 30
```

priya: on the selector side long term: we should change sampling window to ignore streaming prefix for seq_len estimate and add a cheap heuristic: if streaming==true and tool_calls>5, prefer small-kernel unless measured latency improves. also add unit tests for selector edge-cases.

maria: KV cache tweak: make streaming sessions opt-in to stronger retention (avoid eviction until session inactive) — avoids recaching cost when toolloops re-open contexts.

sam: applied pin + batching change at 09:18 UTC. infra-bot confirms action:

infra-bot: ACTION: kernel pinned to pinned:v2 on pool us-west-2-gpu-a at 2026-03-18T09:18:07Z by sam. batching.timeout_ms set to 12 at same time.

infra-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p99 back to 0.45s within 3 minutes, throughput regained to ~95% baseline. eviction rate down to +10% over baseline.

cs-notify-bot: notifying customer-success for tenant acme-inc about temporary throttle and follow-up.

jun: can we avoid customer impact? throttle was small but we should run canary traffic against selector-fix first.

alex: agreed — short-term throttle is minimal and reversible. next steps:
- sam to open PR with selector sampling fix and unit tests (link to issue #1423)
- maria to draft KV-cache retention PR for streaming sessions
- priya to add a lightweight on-host profiler to catch misclassification earlier
- ops to schedule canary rollout of selector changes to us-west-2-gpu-a tomorrow 09:00 UTC

sam: will open PR now and assign reviewers (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987) :thumbsup:

maria: filing follow-up incident note with timeline and flamegraph screenshots.

alex: nice triage team, flagging this as a perf-regression incident candidate. please add postmortem once fixes land. :eyes:

sam: quick status 09:35 UTC — canary: all green, CPU/GPU alloc normal, no further latency spikes. rolling to 3 more pools per rollout plan.
